title: A Butterfly Flaps Its Wings
subtitle: Donning new attire, shedding that thick cocoon—the day my shadow finally eclipses his.

items.text: A Butterfly Flaps Its Wings
Alone in the cemetery, Eagle stands in front of her father's tombstone.
She hadn't been alone long, only a few moments ago a stranger had been there, leaving her with a troubled mind.
It's already difficult enough to keep composed whenever she's here.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: Sorry to keep you waiting, dad.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: Did you hear what he just said? "It isn't too far from Lorentz here."
She crouches over and props up the flowers she brought. Petals from the last time are still caught in the creases of the stone.
Loss makes you age beyond your years—it can't be helped. But maturity has its benefits.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: He said he was your colleague. That you used to be friends.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: Like Matt and his friends?

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: But I don't really understand ...

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: He mentioned Lorentz, and Laplace ... What was that all about? Should I know anything about them?

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: And if I do this, what does that mean? Am I following in your footsteps?

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: I can memorize every word in The Scouts Manual, but ...

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: But I'll never know if I made you proud.
She shakes her head, trying to rid herself of that thought.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: A few days ago, back in Brooklyn, I met someone else.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: He, um ... did I talk about it already?

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: He asked me a question, but I didn't answer. I didn't know how to answer—

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: He asked me, "Want to find something that you can do?"

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: Just like what Mr. X said to me.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: I'm just confused, dad.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: But maybe one day I'll understand, right?
Her gaze turned from the worn old sash in her hands back to the tombstone.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: Right, I will.
She's passing through alleys and over fences, swift as a breath of wind.
It'd been a few days since she and her mom came to visit her aunts. The first thing to do after settling in was to get the lay of the land.
She's learned to do this well, anything to protect her mother and herself.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: Next corner turn right, and then half a block away ...

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: I need to hurry up ...

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: Or mom will get worried.
She leaps lightly into the room, without drawing any attention.
... would be a better place.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: Hi mom, I'm back—Mom?

items.speaker: X
items.text: Oh, hi. Not your mom, but welcome back!

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: Mr. X! Why are you here?

items.speaker: X
items.text: I said see you later. Remember?

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: You—

items.speaker: Mother
items.text: Oh, look at you, your shirt is all wet. Go change out of those clothes. Next time I'll go with you, so you don't get up to trouble.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: Sorry, mom, but there's something ... I need your advice.

items.speaker: Mother
items.text: Alright, but we're drying your hair first.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: I met a man in the cemetery, and he said he worked with dad.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: Do you think you might know him?
She looks over to X as she talks to her mom. X makes a gesture to the door.
Eagle shakes her head disapprovingly.

items.speaker: Mother
items.text: It's possible, sweetie—especially if he recognized you. But, I couldn't say without seeing him myself.

items.speaker: Mother
items.text: But please be careful talking to strangers ... especially with you're out there all alone.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: He told me, father wasn't just in the military, but also a member of "Lorentz."

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: I don't know what that is, but if dad worked there, then maybe ... I can join them instead of the scouts?

items.speaker: Mother
items.text: Sweetheart, all I ever wanted is for you to be healthy and happy.

items.speaker: Mother
items.text: You can join the scouts or Lorentz, or anything! I will support you, no matter what.

items.speaker: X
items.text: Hmm? That sounds like one of my colleagues.

items.speaker: X
items.text: Take this question as the continuation of that conversation.

items.speaker: X
items.text: Would you like to join Laplace with me?

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: I ... I don't know what Laplace and Lorentz are.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: But are girls allowed to join?

items.speaker: X
items.text: Oh, we don't care about any of that. You can join us even if you're neither a boy nor a girl.

items.speaker: X
items.text: But that's really beside the point. As far as you are concerned, Laplace and Lorentz are two different organizations, but we share an office. It's not far from here actually. I can give you a more detailed introduction if you like.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: But my dad is gone. I need to take care of my mom. Besides, we don't live here, so I can't stay long.

items.speaker: X
items.text: Hmm, but your mom just told me you're moving.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: Is that true?

items.speaker: Mother
items.text: Well, your aunties are here, and I want to be closer to your father.

items.speaker: Mother
items.text: Though I still can't bear to go there, but I will one day.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: But, why me? I didn't really help all that much.

items.speaker: X
items.text: Nah, you were a perfect assistant. Remember, you helped me with that equipment, or was that someone else?

items.speaker: X
items.text: Besides, you successfully found "X," both of us, which showed your acute observation skills and capability under pressure.

items.speaker: X
items.text: All in all, I think you'd be wasted on the scouts, you deserve to shine bright, not waste your time collecting tin badges.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: I-I do?

items.speaker: X
items.text: You heard me.

items.speaker: X
items.text: And I'm here to show you another way.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: This is ...

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: A uniform, it's a little like yours!

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: Is this an official uniform?

items.speaker: X
items.text: Yes, and this is the other way I'm offering you.

items.speaker: X
items.text: The way to the Institutum Lorentz.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: Lorentz. Another way ...

items.speaker: X
items.text: That's right.

items.speaker: X
items.text: Because after that mission ...

items.speaker: X
items.text: I think you shouldn't be looking for a puppy, but a butterfly.
THE END
